title: STaR, ReST-EM and Rejection-Sampling Loops: The Filter Is the Model

questions.question: In one iteration of generate -> filter -> train, each strategy's probability in the refit policy is multiplied by what?
options: The strategy's true correctness rate measured on held-out problems
The strategy's acceptance rate under whatever filter the loop uses
The sampling temperature applied when the attempts were generated
The fraction of fresh human-written data mixed into the training set
questions.explanation: SFT on the kept set reproduces its strategy mix, so pi'(s) is proportional to pi(s) times a_s, the acceptance rate. Correctness enters only through the filter, which is why the filter is the model.

questions.question: A symmetric noisy filter accepts correct samples with probability TPR and wrong samples with probability q. When does the less-correct strategy's share grow?
options: Whenever q is above zero, since any accepted wrong sample teaches the wrong strategy
When q exceeds the false-negative rate, so accepted wrongs outnumber rejected corrects
When the shortcut's correctness c_B is above one half on the training problem pool
Only when q exceeds TPR, because a_s = q + (TPR - q) c_s is then decreasing in c_s
questions.explanation: Acceptance is affine in correctness with slope TPR - q, so the ordering of strategies by acceptance matches their ordering by correctness unless q > TPR. A uniform leak slows and contaminates the loop; it does not reverse it.

questions.question: Why can a filter that is informative on average (TPR well above q) still amplify a wrong strategy?
options: Its false positives concentrate on that strategy's plausible wrong answers, so a_B exceeds a_A
Its false negatives remove the right strategy's correct answers faster than the wrong one's
Add-one smoothing on the strategy counts keeps the wrong strategy from ever shrinking
Retraining from the base model each round discards whatever the previous round learned
questions.explanation: Real filters leak non-uniformly: tests miss exactly the edge cases a shortcut fails on, judges favour confident prose. Once the extra leak b on the shortcut's plausible wrong answers exceeds b* = (TPR - q)(c_A - c_B) / P(plausible wrong | B), the shortcut's acceptance rate is the higher one.

questions.question: In the simulator the self-assessment filter drives the shortcut's share from 50% to 99% while accuracy falls. What causes this?
options: The threshold tau is so low that almost every attempt is accepted regardless of strategy
The shortcut is correct more often than the general method on puzzles without a clause
Confidence barely tracks correctness and the shortcut sounds more confident, so a_B > a_A
The general method's skill falls as it trains on its own wrong executions each round
questions.explanation: Self-assessment accepts by P(confidence > tau | s). With a weak confidence-correctness link and a higher confidence baseline for the shortcut, the shortcut's acceptance (0.77) beats the method's (0.39), so its odds double every iteration.

questions.question: Which placement on the verification hierarchy predicts the weakest and least trustworthy self-improvement, and why?
options: Execution tests, because coverage gaps leak the shortcut's edge-case failures into training
Intrinsic self-assessment, because the loop then converges to the most confident output mode
Answer matching, because it is silent on every problem the model has never solved
Formal verification, because so few domains can be fully formalized in a proof assistant
questions.explanation: Chen et al. (2026) rank formal verifiers strongest and intrinsic self-assessment weakest, and report that demonstrated self-improvement strength follows the order. At the bottom tier acceptance is P(confident), which need not track correctness at all.

questions.question: A team reports that accepted-sample counts rise each iteration and training loss falls, and calls the loop healthy. What does this lesson say they must also report?
options: The sampling temperature and the number of samples drawn per prompt in each iteration
The total compute spent on generation compared with the compute spent on training
The size of the base model and whether it was retrained from scratch in every round
Filter precision on a held-out truth set per iteration and acceptance rates per output mode
questions.explanation: Accepted counts and loss rise under a degenerating loop too (self-assessment: 1,113 -> 1,492 accepted while accuracy fell to 36%). Only an audit against truth the loop cannot see, plus per-mode acceptance rates, reveals contamination and the growth condition.
